# Footprint Finder

> Footprint Finder scans your inbox to find every account, breach, and data-broker listing tied to your email — then helps you delete or opt out. Free scan, monthly rescans, real-time alerts.

Footprint Finder is a privacy management service for individuals. It uses read-only OAuth metadata (sender, subject, date — never message body) to discover services where your email is registered, classifies them by activity and risk, and provides one-click cleanup actions (delete account, unsubscribe, opt out under CCPA). On the Complete plan, data-broker scans surface where your name, address, and phone are publicly listed across 25+ US people-search sites.

## Plans

- Free — 1 email account, 3 deletion requests/month, breach check. No data-broker scanning.
- Pro — $79/year or $12.99/month. Up to 3 email accounts, unlimited deletion requests, deep inbox scan, monthly rescans. No data-broker scanning.
- Complete — $129/year or $19.99/month. Everything in Pro, plus data-broker scanning and removal across 25+ sites, and up to 5 email accounts.
- Family — $179/year. Everything in Complete, for up to 5 people.
- Parent Protection Scan — $39 one-time. A single deep scan of a parent's email, scam-focused, no subscription.

Data-broker removal is a Complete-tier feature. Pro does not include it.

## Pages

- [Home](/): Overview, free scan entry point, pricing summary.
- [Free Scan](/free-scan): Instant breach + exposure check by email (no account required).
- [Pricing](/pricing): Full plan comparison.
- [Parent Scan](/parents): One-time $39 scan for an elderly parent's email (scam-focused).
- [Enterprise](/enterprise): Shadow IT audits and B2B offering.
- [Best Data Removal Services](/best-data-removal-services): All 10 services ranked by category, with the honest catch for each — including ours.
- [Compare](/vs): Alternatives pages for DeleteMe, Incogni, OneRep, Privacy Bee, EasyOptOuts, Aura, Optery, Kanary and Mine, plus head-to-head pages such as /vs/deleteme-vs-incogni.
- [Data-Broker Removal Guides](/remove-from): Free opt-out instructions for 45+ US brokers.
- [California DROP Guide](/guides/california-drop-delete-act): How California residents delete their data from every state-registered broker with one free request, what DROP does not cover, and the 1 August 2026 broker compliance deadline.
- [Removal Plan Builder](/plan): Free interactive tool that builds a personalised, ordered removal checklist from your state, situation and concerns. No email or account required; plans are shareable via URL parameters (e.g. /plan?state=texas&for=seniors) and printable.
- [Removal Guidance by Situation](/for): Situation-specific guidance for domestic violence survivors, law enforcement and judges (Daniel's Law-style takedown rights), healthcare workers, teachers, journalists, seniors, job seekers and content creators. Each leads with the strongest protection available to that group, including free state programmes that beat paid services.
- [Privacy Rights by State](/privacy-rights): What deletion rights residents of each of the 50 states plus DC actually have — 20 states with comprehensive laws, 4 with broker registries, 1 (California) with a centralised deletion platform.
- [Remove Data by Type](/remove): Removal guides for specific categories — Social Security number, date of birth, relatives, mugshots, court records, property records, voter registration, address history — each stating plainly what cannot be removed.
- [What Big Tech Knows About You](/what-they-know): What Google, Facebook, Amazon, TikTok, Apple, LinkedIn, Instagram, Microsoft, Uber and Spotify each hold on you, how to download your own copy from each company's official export tool, how to limit future collection, and what each one retains after account deletion. Distinct from broker removal: this covers accounts the user opened themselves, which no data-broker removal service examines.
- [Privacy Guides](/guides): How-to guides for removing your name, address, phone number, email and images from the internet and from Google.
- [Account Deletion Guides](/delete): Step-by-step instructions for permanently deleting accounts on Facebook, Instagram, Amazon, LinkedIn, Spotify and more.
- [Breach Pages](/breach): Plain-English explainers for 16 major data breaches — Equifax, Yahoo, Marriott/Starwood, T-Mobile, Capital One, Facebook, LinkedIn, 23andMe, MOVEit, Change Healthcare, AT&T, Ticketmaster, Anthem, Adobe, Uber, MyFitnessPal, National Public Data. Each covers what happened, the confirmed data classes exposed, why it still matters years later rather than only on the day it broke, settlement history where applicable, and the response that matches that specific kind of data. Settlement claim windows are described in the past tense because they have closed.
- [Browser Extension](/extension): Chrome extension for in-context cleanup.
- [Help](/help): FAQ explaining server-side metadata scanning.
- [Demo](/demo): Interactive demo with sample data.
